key_insight: Microstructure-dependent recurrent neural operators can approximate homogenized Kelvin–Voigt constitutive laws uniformly across time, admissible loading histories, and material fields in 2D and 3D.
engineering_relevance: These surrogates aim to replace costly concurrent unit-cell simulations while retaining microstructure-dependent, history-sensitive material responses.
method: Encode loading-history dependence with Markovian internal variables.
Learn microstructure-dependent constitutive responses using neural operators.
Use spectral memory-kernel approximation to bound sufficient internal-variable dimension logarithmically in inverse relative stress error and material contrast.
evidence_signal: Unit-cell-data experiments on viscoelasticity and crystal plasticity examine internal-variable dimension and sample complexity; theoretical results are formally verified in Lean 4.
watch_item: The approximation guarantee covers periodic Kelvin–Voigt viscoelasticity, not general nonlinear inelasticity; crystal plasticity is supported by numerical experiments.
paper_title: Operator Learning of Microstructure-Dependent Internal-Variable Models for Inelastic Homogenization: Approximation and Complexity
